prize_name: Stein Rokkan Prize for Comparative Social Science Research
awarding_org: European Consortium for Political Research (ECPR), jointly with the International Science Council and the University of Bergen
funder_origin_name: International Social Science Council and Conjunto Universitario Candido Mendes
funding_share_basis: The prize was instituted jointly in 1981 by the International Social Science Council (ISSC, seated in Paris, France) and the Conjunto Universitario Candido Mendes (Rio de Janeiro, Brazil), which co-financed and co-awarded it until 2002; no split between the two was ever published, so both the origin type and the origin country are Mixed, with France and Brazil as the component countries. Today the University of Bergen supplies the entire purse (GBP 4,300 / EUR 5,000, previously USD 5,000) and has done so since 2008, while ECPR and the ISC (successor to the ISSC after its 2018 merger with ICSU) contribute administration and the jury but no purse money. Applying the >50% test to the money, 100% of what the winner receives today is new Bergen money and none of it comes from the 1981 founders' funds, so funder_changed is true.
money_note: Current purse GBP 4,300 (quoted elsewhere as EUR 5,000; previously USD 5,000), paid in full by the University of Bergen since 2008.
status_note: Continuously awarded under the same name since 1981, but irregularly (roughly biennially) until 2008 and annually since; winner lists therefore have genuine gap years (e.g. 1982, 1984-85, 1987, 1989, 1991, 1993-95, 1997, 1999, 2001, 2003, 2005, 2007). The co-founding Brazilian partner (Conjunto Universitario Candido Mendes) ceased co-awarding after 2002, and the ISSC became the International Science Council in its 2018 merger with ICSU.
evidence_quote: The Prize was instituted jointly by the ISSC and the Conjunto Universitario Candido Mendes in Brazil... Since 2008, and thanks to the generous support of the University of Bergen... the Stein Rokkan Prize amounts to $US 5000.
judgment_reason: The prize is presented jointly by three bodies, so awarding_org could equally be coded as the International Science Council (International, France), which hosts the prize pages and announcements, or the University of Bergen (University, Norway); I chose ECPR because it runs the process end to end - nominations go to prizes@ecpr.eu and the jury is chaired by an ECPR Executive Committee member - and coded it Society (UK-registered charity, secretariat in Colchester) rather than International, since its members are individual universities and departments rather than national organizations. Origin funding is coded Mixed in both type and country because the 1981 founding partners (ISSC in France, Conjunto Universitario Candido Mendes in Brazil) are named jointly with no documented majority share; a coder who read the ISSC as the senior partner would code France instead.
